pool.text: Lifeboat station was established to aid maritime rescue operations in Holyhead.
Parliamentary borough created covering the town area as part of Beaumaris Boroughs.
Mail service through Holyhead temporarily suspended in favor of Liverpool rail route.
Holyhead lost the London‑Dublin mail contract to Liverpool port.
Construction of substantial breakwater began, continuing into the 1870s.
Soldiers Point Hotel constructed as residence for harbour alteration engineer.
North Wales coastal railway opened, reinstating Irish Mail service at Holyhead.
Chester and Holyhead Railway completed, enabling new Holyhead railway station.
National Eisteddfod held in Holyhead, showcasing Welsh arts and literature.
Holyhead Urban District abolished; area became a community under county council.
Holyhead Rural parish renamed Trearddur, reflecting local identity.
Census reported 47% of Holyhead residents able to speak Welsh.
Aluminium smelter ceased operations, ending Holyhead's main industrial activity.
British government listed Wylfa as potential future nuclear power station site.
Soldiers Point Hotel badly damaged by fire, impacting historic building.
Census showed 52.2% of Welsh‑born residents could speak Welsh.
Holyhead & Anglesey Amateur Boxing Club founded, promoting local sport.
Holyhead officially twinned with Greystones, County Wicklow, Ireland.
Port remained second busiest UK roll‑on roll‑off hub until end of year.
Freight traffic from Ireland dropped by half following Brexit agreement.
